pr_title: Always use same protocol for clone remotes
pr_body:
This PR makes it so when we add an `upstream` remote during `repo clone` the URL uses the same protocol as the `origin` remote. If the clone URL does not include the protocol to use we only need to checks the users `git_protocol` preference once since a repo parent has to come from the same host as the fork.

In #5984 the user had `ssh` `git_protocol` configured for "github.com" and `https` `git_protocol` as the normal default, so in some odd circumstances when the `canonicalRepo.Parent.RepoHost()` did not return the same host as `repo.RepoHost()` it caused us to write different protocols for the `upstream` and `origin` remotes. 

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5984
pr_comments: I no longer believe this is  the correct fix for this issue.

issue_context.title: Repo clone: warn about existing upstream remote
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

I am using version 2.12.1 of GitHub CLI on Monterey 12.5 (updated recently, in case that is relevant).

When I clone my fork using the regular long-form git clone, all is well - discovered this when trying to debug what was behind the issues.

If I clone my fork with gh repo clone <my fork> (which I do all the time) just recently I started to get some issues:

```
ruth.cheesley@MacBookPro-RuthCheesley local.mautictest % gh repo clone rcheesley/mautic
Cloning into 'mautic'...
remote: Enumerating objects: 285261, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (59/59), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (36/36), done.
remote: Total 285261 (delta 40), reused 39 (delta 23), pack-reused 285202
Receiving objects: 100% (285261/285261), 146.90 MiB | 5.46 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (204241/204241), done.
Updating files: 100% (7205/7205), done.
error: remote upstream already exists.
exit status 3
```
The remotes are seemingly set as below:
```
ruth.cheesley@MacBookPro-RuthCheesley mautic % git remote -v
origin  git@github.com:RCheesley/mautic.git (fetch)
origin  git@github.com:RCheesley/mautic.git (push)
upstream        https://github.com/mautic/mautic.git (fetch)
upstream        https://github.com/mautic/mautic.git (push)
```
From this point forward I am unable to do anything with the upstream repo:

```
ruth.cheesley@MacBookPro-RuthCheesley mautic % git fetch upstream
fatal: unable to connect to [github.com](http://github.com/):
[github.com](http://github.com/)[0: 140.82.121.4]: errno=Operation timed out

ruth.cheesley@MacBookPro-RuthCheesley mautic % gh pr checkout 11348
? Which should be the base repository (used for e.g. querying issues) for this directory? mautic/mautic
fatal: unable to connect to [github.com](http://github.com/):
[github.com](http://github.com/)[0: 140.82.121.3]: errno=Operation timed out
```

If I check out with the regular git clone command the remotes are fine, both are using the same format. If I set the remote for the clone from CLI from https to the same format as the origin then all is well.

I have used the CLI command many times to clone the fork so it seems like a relatively new thing, but I can't seem to get to the bottom of what is causing the remotes to be different when using the CLI. Bit of a pain to have to update every time!

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Clone a fork without using the CLI and check the remotes are in the same format
2. Clone the same fork using the CLI and in my case the origin and upstream are in different formats, and the upstream does not work until I change the format.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Should be able to work with the upstream repo as usual without modifying the remotes.

### Logs

`[2022-07-22 16:08:57.382] [GIT  ] [/Users/ruth.cheesley/Sites/local.mautictest/mautic] git fetch upstream • Command failed: /opt/homebrew/bin/git -c core.quotepath=false -c color.ui=false fetch upstream • unable to connect to github.com: • github.com[0: 140.82.121.4]: errno=Operation timed out • 17066 ms (slow)`

Sure, `gh repo clone` sets up 2 git remotes for repos that are forks, but a regular `git clone` always just sets up 1 git remote (in my experience) and doesn't know anything about the relationship of GitHub repositories. That's why I'm puzzled by the behavior on your system.

Hi, just updating this to make a note that I wasn't able to discover any way of how `git clone` could have produced 2 remotes (incl. "upstream") instead of one ("origin"). But, maybe we could amend the `gh repo clone` implementation to gracefully exit with a warning (instead of erroring out) if an `upstream` remote already exists. It shouldn't be hard to do and it would cover strange cases like these, even if we don't understand what causes this. Contributions welcome!

review_comments:
Something that could be a potential regression after this change is that the per-host `git_protocol` configuration for the upstream remote won't be respected anymore, in case someone relied on this behavior:
```sh
gh repo clone myprotocol://github.com/owner/repo #=> uses "myprotocol" for origin remote
#=> "upstream" remote is configured by respecting git_protocol like in the rest of gh
```
Could we instead investigate why `canonicalRepo.Parent.RepoHost()` wasn't `github.com` for this user?
